messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — runtime-prod (us-east1) high queue depth detected. 5m error rate breach. https://internal.incidents/redwood/3600123456 :rotating_light:

sasha: Got it — I'm oncall. Pulling metrics and runbooks now.

miguel: Observability: sudden tail latency + inflight spike. inflight ~1250 (baseline ~420). worker queue backlog growing, CPU on some hosts spiking. No obvious model change. Likely traffic surge from a misbehaving client or cached KV misses.

sasha: +1. Quick mitigation options: lower max_inflight for public tier, enable soft-shedding for best-effort routes, tighten per-API-key rate limits, or temporarily disable non-essential features (e.g. rerank route). Which do we want first?

harper: Recommend quick, reversible changes in this order:
1) set max_inflight public -> 300
2) enable 15% soft-shedding on best-effort route group
3) increase request timeout to 40s to avoid partial work thrash
4) if still bad, throttle anonymous/unverified keys by 3x.

rina: Any high-value customers impacted? I can check billing tags.

miguel: Telemetry snapshot: 2 high-commit customers (acct-A, acct-B) saw a small spike in 429s (~3-5%) and latency increase. Most spikes are from untagged traffic (unknown API keys) — probably a bot.

sasha: I'm going to apply step 1 and 2 now. Posting the admin API call I'm about to run:

```
curl -X POST https://admin.internal/configs/runtime/traffic -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' -d '{"max_inflight": {"public": 300}, "shedding": {"best_effort_ratio": 0.15}}'
```

ops-bot: CONFIG-CHANGE logged: config_id=cfg-20260315-01 author=sasha scope=runtime/us-east1 diff="max_inflight.public: 420->300; shedding.best_effort_ratio: 0.0->0.15"

incident-bot: NOTE — mitigation applied by sasha at 2026-03-15T14:12:30Z. Auto-checking queue depth in 60s.

miguel: Initial impact within 2 minutes: queue depth down ~35%, inflight ~480, tail latency improving. 429s for unknown keys up ~6% (expected), committed customers stable.

rina: Noted. Reached out to acct-A; they report a few failed requests but no customer-facing outages. acct-B on standby, but wants notification if we throttle further.

sasha: OK handing off primary pager to harper for monitoring and further action. harper — you're live.

harper: Ack, taking over. I'll keep the shedding config for 30m and watch error budgets. If queue depth falls below 120 for 10m, we'll stepwise relax: shedding -> 10% -> 5% -> 0, max_inflight -> 420.

harper: Adding a temporary traffic-shaper to reduce anonymous burst to 10rps per key:
```
adminctl shaper apply --scope runtime/us-east1 --match "tag:anonymous" --rate 10
```

ops-bot: SHAPER-APPLY queued by harper. change_id=shp-3600123456-1

incident-bot: UPDATE — after both mitigations: severity lowered to S2, customer-impact = partial (throttled unknown keys, degraded latency for heavy requests).

miguel: Follow-ups: 1) run a quick analysis to identify upstream bot patterns, block offending API keys; 2) prepare an action to rollback if any committed customer's errors exceed 1%.

sasha: I'll create an incident ticket with current mitigations + timeline and tag infra/sec for postmortem.

rina: I'll keep comms ready in case acct-B requests escalation.

harper: Monitoring greenline: queue depth now 90, inflight 320, tail p95 ~780ms. Keeping config for 18 more minutes, then will relax if stable.

incident-bot: RESOLVE-READY check scheduled in 20m.

mina: small follow-up — please add the runbook step we used to the playbook: "apply anonymous shaper then soft-shedding" (I know it's minor but saved time).

sasha: Will add. Closing handoff chat. harper continues watch. :white_check_mark:
